target_customer: Accounting and finance leaders at software companies that must capitalize software development costs
problem: Accounting teams chase engineers for timesheets or quarterly surveys to decide which software work can be capitalized, and issue trackers like Jira alone have incomplete data.
business_model: B2B SaaS integrated with developer tools (pricing not found)
product_category: Finance automation: software R&D cost capitalization

founders.name: Neha Shah
founders.background_notes: YC page and launch post: product manager at Affirm building traceability and reporting for daily money movements. Education not listed.

founders.name: Jay Gokhale
founders.background_notes: YC page: product engineer at Stripe for nearly five years on regulated fintech products. Education not listed.

competitors.name: Jellyfish (DevFinOps)
competitors.what: Engineering management platform that launched an R&D cost capitalization reporting product
competitors.traction_then: generally available on launch day, with customers such as Iterable using it

technical_complexity.rationale: Pulling data from Jira and developer workflows and mapping it to capitalization rules is integration work with accounting domain rules, not research grade engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Audit trails and accounting workflows can create stickiness, but a funded engineering analytics vendor already shipped a similar product three months before the batch.

incumbents: Jira and other engineering analytics tools
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Jellyfish launched DevFinOps in October 2022. No source records Mogara's response or any acquisition.

market_need_then: US tax rules for tax years after 2021 required capitalizing and amortizing domestic R&E costs including software, creating compliance work. The launch post cites manual surveys as the incumbent process.

branding.domain_note: Uses mogara.com. No purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and benefit led: automatic software R&D capitalization

brand_strength.rationale: No source on the name, logo or community was found, and the invented name gives no hint of the finance use case.

outcome_analysis: Mogara addressed a real compliance pain after the 2022 R&E amortization change, but a funded rival, Jellyfish, launched a capitalization product in October 2022. The company is listed inactive in the YC directory with a single reported $500K early round and no later funding. No shutdown notice or post-mortem was found and the website returned HTTP 503, so the cause is not public.
notes: Two aggregators report one $500K round: CB Insights as a convertible note dated 2023-01-01 with Y Combinator, FundedIQ as pre-seed dated 2023-04-05 with no investors. The stage is recorded as other because they conflict; $500K matches the amount typically reported for the standard YC deal but no source says so. Founder technical flags come from the described roles. Website returned HTTP 503. Exit type unknown because YC status Inactive has no shutdown source.
